title: BoJ Tankan (December 2026 survey) — the one Tankan a year that is NOT the first trading day of a quarter
source: EST: boj.or.jp/en/statistics/outline/tkohyos.xlsx ('Schedule for Releases of Statistical Data (From July 2026 to June 2027)', linked from boj.or.jp/en/statistics/outline/), re-fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 48,500 bytes), unzipped and parsed cell-by-cell out of its 'Statistics data' sheet by this session. Row 230 gives the Dec.-Survey column of 'Tankan (Short-Term Economic Survey of Enterprises in Japan) / Summary and Outline' at '8:50 a.m.', and row 231 gives that column's date as Excel serial 46370 = 2026-12-14; the same row's June-survey cell is serial 46204 = 2026-07-01, which matches the June 2026 survey's ALREADY-PUBLISHED release date on boj.or.jp/en/statistics/tk/ ('July 1, 2026 | June 2026 Survey'), so the serial decoding is validated against an observed release rather than assumed. Rows 232-235 put the Comprehensive Data Set and Long-Term Time-Series Data one day later, serial 46371 = 2026-12-15. Release time corroborated verbatim from the Bank's own methodology page boj.or.jp/en/statistics/outline/exp/tk/extk.htm (HTTP 200, 66,232 bytes): 'The survey results are released at the beginning of April, July, October, and mid-December in principle (released at 8:50 a.m. Japan Standard Time).' Consistent with the Bank's own TANKAN (Summary) archives (boj.or.jp/en/statistics/tk/gaiyo/{2001,2006,2011,2016,2021,2026}/index.htm, HTTP 200 each, 90 release dates parsed by this session): every December survey since 2004 has published between the 13th and the 16th of December, 22/22 (2004-12-15, 2005-12-14, 2006-12-15, 2007-12-14, 2008-12-15, 2009-12-14, 2010-12-15, 2011-12-15, 2012-12-14, 2013-12-16, 2014-12-15, 2015-12-14, 2016-12-14, 2017-12-15, 2018-12-14, 2019-12-13, 2020-12-14, 2021-12-13, 2022-12-14, 2023-12-13, 2024-12-13, 2025-12-15), and JPX's own market calendar (jpx.co.jp/english/corporate/about-jpx/calendar/, HTTP 200, 33,103 bytes, its holiday table parsed row by row today) lists no December 2026 Tokyo closure before Dec. 31, so Monday 2026-12-14 is an ordinary trading session. Filed estimate on two counts, identical to the thirteen BoJ entries already on this calendar: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has FED: for the Federal Reserve and no slot for the Bank of Japan, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep.
notes: DISCOVERED during the boj-tankan-2026-10-01 initial-research sweep (2026-09-05) and filed because it is the ONLY clean measurement this calendar can make on the Tankan. The March, June and September surveys all publish on the first business day of April, July and October — i.e. the first trading day of a quarter — so a Tankan effect and a quarter-start effect are perfectly collinear on those dates. Across 2004-2026 there are exactly two April/July/October quarter-start sessions without a Tankan (2010-10-01, because the 2010 September survey printed on 09-29; and 2020-10-02, because the Tokyo Stock Exchange halted the whole of 10-01), so n=2 identifies nothing. The mid-December survey carries no quarter boundary, which makes it the one structurally clean cut — and it runs a Nikkei opening gap of 0.399% median = 0.80x an ordinary session, p = 0.34, n=22. That is why boj-tankan-2026-10-01's third forward test (FT-boj-tankan-2026-10-01-3) is scored on THIS date rather than on its own: a December gap above the n=89 detection floor of 0.641% is the first observation that would genuinely re-open the channel that ledger closes. AMENDED by this event's own initial research on 2026-09-05 (docs/research/events/boj-tankan-2026-12-14.md), which measured the cut and found it is NOT clean — it swaps one perfect confound for another. The 0.80x is a denominator artifact: against DECEMBER's own sessions the cut runs 0.94x (p = 0.77), because all December sessions run 0.85x (p = 0.010, n=437). And the release is collinear with the BoJ's own decision — all 22 December Tankans since 2004 published 2-6 calendar days before that year's December MPM decision statement (22/22), the 8 that fell on a Monday all sat at exactly MPM-4, and 2026-12-14 (Monday) -> 2026-12-18 (Friday decision) repeats that configuration. December sessions at MPM-4 run 2.02x the December pool (p = 0.003) and 1.76x with every Tankan day removed (n=6, p = 0.082); only 2 of the 10 December Mondays at MPM-4 carry no Tankan, which is the identical n=2 identification failure that made the September cut unusable. Consequence: the 0.641% threshold's breach rate on the cell this date occupies is 0.600 (6/10), not the 0.396 all-session figure it was calibrated on. Impact is MEDIUM, matching the September entry: the Tankan is a Statistics-Law survey of a ~210,000-enterprise population (9,141 respondents at a 99.37% response rate in the June 2026 release), so it is a first-release statistical print rather than an anonymised digest — but symbols is empty, no house playbook is rates- or FX-keyed, and this calendar measures no Tankan channel to the Nikkei open (0.88x over 90 releases), the S&P (1.03x) or the yen (0.98x). The corridor around this date is already crowded and separately owned: boj-decision-2026-12-18 and japan-cpi-2026-12-18 sit four days later, so nothing on the 12-18 tape is attributable to this survey without ruling those out first. Precedent for filing a non-MPM Bank of Japan statistical release as its own entry: japan-cpi-2026-12-18, kind 'macro-print'.
